headline: Government brings back citizenship bill for 2,055 approved applicants
deck: Each applicant will be checked again; Venstre, which backed the bill in February, now wants it to wait.
standard: The government will bring back a bill granting citizenship to 2,055 previously approved applicants and their children in the first half of 2027, Morten Bødskov, the immigration and integration minister, said on Monday. It lapsed when an election was called.
Each applicant will first be checked again, and some may be dropped. They will not face the values screening the government wants for other applicants, which an expert group is still studying.

Venstre, a liberal party, backed the bill in February. On Monday its leader, Troels Lund Poulsen, wrote that the government should wait for the screening. Liberal Alliance, a libertarian party, calls it a 'gigantic broken promise'.
short: The government will bring back a bill granting citizenship to 2,055 previously approved applicants after a fresh check of each, Morten Bødskov, the immigration and integration minister, said on Monday. Venstre, a liberal party, backed the bill in February but now wants the government to wait for a values screening.
